TON.purpose_en: Delay turning a timer contact On while the input remains On.
behavior_en: Current value increases while enabled; the contact turns On when the preset is reached.
Input Off or RST clears the contact and resets the current value to zero.
constraints_en: T selects the timer device; t is its WORD preset. The delay is the preset multiplied by the base time configured for that timer number.
Available base times are 0.1 ms, 1 ms, 10 ms, and 100 ms; XGB does not support 0.1 ms.
The same timer number cannot be used twice, even when indexed. Indexed timer/preset operands are limited to Z0..Z3; an indexed RST must match the timer operand form.

TOFF.purpose_en: Keep a timer contact On for the preset interval after the input turns Off.
behavior_en: Input On loads the preset and turns the contact On.
After input Off, the value counts down; zero turns the contact Off. RST clears the contact and value.
constraints_en: T selects the timer device; t is its WORD preset. The delay is the preset multiplied by the base time configured for that timer number.
Available base times are 0.1 ms, 1 ms, 10 ms, and 100 ms; XGB does not support 0.1 ms.
The same timer number cannot be used twice, even when indexed. Indexed timer/preset operands are limited to Z0..Z3; an indexed RST must match the timer operand form.

TMR.purpose_en: Accumulate enabled time across separate On intervals.
behavior_en: The value increases while the input is On and is retained while Off; reaching the preset turns the contact On.
RST clears the contact and current value. Power-loss retention requires a nonvolatile timer area.
constraints_en: T selects the timer device; t is its WORD preset. The delay is the preset multiplied by the base time configured for that timer number.
Available base times are 0.1 ms, 1 ms, 10 ms, and 100 ms; XGB does not support 0.1 ms.
The same timer number cannot be used twice, even when indexed. Indexed timer/preset operands are limited to Z0..Z3; an indexed RST must match the timer operand form.

TMON.purpose_en: Produce a non-retriggered monostable timer interval.
behavior_en: Input On turns the contact On and starts counting down from the preset.
After starting, input On/Off changes do not interrupt the countdown. Zero turns the contact Off; RST clears the output and value.
constraints_en: T selects the timer device; t is its WORD preset. The delay is the preset multiplied by the base time configured for that timer number.
Available base times are 0.1 ms, 1 ms, 10 ms, and 100 ms; XGB does not support 0.1 ms.
The same timer number cannot be used twice, even when indexed. Indexed timer/preset operands are limited to Z0..Z3; an indexed RST must match the timer operand form.
review_notes: The initial instruction/device table incorrectly says TMR. The page title, function description, and timer overview identify TMON.

TRTG.purpose_en: Produce a timer pulse whose duration restarts on a new rising input.
behavior_en: Input On starts the contact and countdown from the preset.
A new Off-to-On input before zero reloads the preset. Zero or RST turns the contact Off; RST also clears the value.
constraints_en: T selects the timer device; t is its WORD preset. The delay is the preset multiplied by the base time configured for that timer number.
Available base times are 0.1 ms, 1 ms, 10 ms, and 100 ms; XGB does not support 0.1 ms.
The same timer number cannot be used twice, even when indexed. Indexed timer/preset operands are limited to Z0..Z3; an indexed RST must match the timer operand form.

behavior_en: Each rising pulse increments the current value by one. The contact is On when the value reaches or exceeds N; counting continues up to 65,535.
RST clears the contact and current value.
constraints_en: C selects a counter device; N is a WORD preset in 0..65,535.

CTD.purpose_en: Count rising inputs downward from a preset.
behavior_en: Each rising pulse decrements the current value; zero turns the contact On.
RST clears the contact and restores the current value to N.
constraints_en: C selects a counter device; N is a WORD preset in 0..65,535.

CTUD.purpose_en: Count separate up and down rising pulses.
behavior_en: A rising U increments the count; a rising D decrements it. Simultaneous rising U and D leave the count unchanged.
The contact is On when the current value reaches or exceeds N. RST resets the count to zero.
The instruction enable must remain On for up/down counting.
constraints_en: C selects a counter device; U and D are BIT operands; N is a WORD preset in 0..65,535.
review_notes: A decrement symbol in the Korean body is corrupted as ?1; the D operand description and example identify decrement by one.

Ti is an integral time denominator: reducing it strengthens integral action.
constraints_en: XGK and XGB use different K-device layouts. Preserve user-read-only/reserved parameter entries.
When deleting PIDRUN through a RUN-time edit, first turn its enable contact Off; otherwise the previous output may remain and a later insertion can resume the loop.
review_notes: The second PID parameter table is labelled XGK but contains XGB K1200-based data; distinguish it from the XGK K1000-based layout.

S+0 holds SV (WORD), S+1 Ts (WORD, 0.1 ms), S+2 Kp (REAL), S+4 Ti (REAL), and S+6 Td (REAL). D is the constant loop number.
constraints_en: The page documents D in 0..31; check the selected CPU family rather than extending XGB beyond its supported loop range.

PIDPAUSE.purpose_en: Pause a running PID loop while preserving its state.

constraints_en: Avoid direct competing writes to the same _PIDn_PAUSE bit. The manual cautions that long pauses or unstable/noisy systems can destabilize control.

The manual lists Cnet V3.2/CPU V4.2 and FEnet V8.0/CPU V4.7 minimums. A prior unfinished same-slot request is reported in status; inspect status instead of assuming synchronous completion.

RCVUDATA.purpose_en: Receive user-defined data through a configured Cnet/FEnet channel.
behavior_en: sl selects h00xy; S1 is Cnet channel 1/2 or a user-defined FEnet P2P channel. D1 is the destination and D2 reports the received byte count.
D3..D3+3 is the four-WORD internal/status workspace. Data exceeding 1,024 bytes raises status 08 and only 1,024 bytes are stored.
constraints_en: Initialize the workspace to zero; do not reuse or manually alter it. Reserve enough destination devices and require user-defined parameters/link enable.
The manual lists Cnet V3.2/CPU V4.2 and FEnet V8.0/CPU V4.7 minimums. The page says prior-command status 09 is XGB-only.

SETIP.purpose_en: Set CPU local-Ethernet IP, mask and gateway together.
behavior_en: S1, S2 and S3 point to four WORDs each, with one decimal IPv4 octet per WORD. To change only IP, first read the existing mask/gateway with GETIP.
constraints_en: Only CPUs with local Ethernet support this instruction. Invalid addresses/parameters or specified DHCP configurations set F110.

MSETIP.purpose_en: Set a FEnet module IP, mask and gateway together.
behavior_en: sl selects the module; S1/S2/S3 each point to four WORDs containing one IPv4 octet per WORD. Preserve mask/gateway with MNETINFO when changing only IP.
D..D+2 holds status, internal WAIT/DONE state, and retry count; do not overwrite it.
constraints_en: DHCP prevents this IP change. The status table requires FEnet V8.1; confirm the CPU/tool versions listed in the source.
review_notes: The example says decimal 100 equals 0x00C8; correct conversion is 0x0064. The ST example incorrectly calls MNETINFO_EN; do not copy it as MSETIP syntax.

SST.purpose_en: Start configured APM positioning steps on multiple axes simultaneously.
behavior_en: Use n1/n2/n3 for X/Y/Z step numbers and n4 as the axis-selection bitmask. Two or more valid axes must participate.
constraints_en: The page ax convention is 0=X,1=Y,2=Z for XGF-PxxA; verify the actual module axis count. XGB has no Z operand use, fixes n4 to 3, and has its own step limits.
Invalid participating axis data can prevent all selected axes from starting.
review_notes: The n4 table only labels bits 0..2, but its h000B example selects four-axis data. Use the actual module manual when fourth-axis behavior matters.

XSST.purpose_en: Start previously configured XPM steps on multiple axes simultaneously.
behavior_en: ax is the command axis (1..8 for XGF-PN8B); n1 is the axis mask with bit0=axis1 through bit7=axis8. The command axis participates even if absent from the mask.
Configure each participating axis simultaneous-start step with XSWR or PUT/PUTP before executing XSST.
constraints_en: At least two valid axes must participate. Module axis-count/range or step-data errors can prevent the complete start. XBC-U/XBM can use XBF-PNxxB in slots 2/3 only.

PWM.purpose_en: Emit a pulse train with a configured period and Off duty on XGB built-in positioning.
behavior_en: ax=0/1 selects X/Y; n1 is the period in 1..20,000 ms; n2 is Off duty 0..100 percent. Pulses run while the enable is On without updating current position.

The body describes XGB built-in positioning and lists CPU hardware/OS minimums; do not assume every CPU in the broad heading supports it.
review_notes: The introductory sentence describes position movement and is copied from another instruction. The function section defines PWM and Off duty.
The example also refers to DST absolute/relative position settings; this is copied position-operation prose, not a condition for the PWM duty/period instruction.

XTRUN.purpose_en: Issue motion-module test operations while the module is STOP.

SET Syyy.xx.purpose_en: Advance a step relay group in sequential order.
behavior_en: The target step turns On only while the immediately preceding step in the same group is On and the target input is On; the preceding step then turns Off.
The active step latches even after input Off. Only one step is active in a group.
At initial RUN, Syyy.00 is On; enabling Syyy.00 clears the sequential group.
constraints_en: yyy is the group number 0..127 and xx is the step number 0..99. The operand is a BIT step-relay contact.
review_notes: This is the S-device sequential-control instruction; do not equate its mnemonic template with arbitrary SFC graph-step insertion.

OUT Syyy.xx.purpose_en: Select a latched step relay using the last enabled instruction in program order.
behavior_en: An input On activates its step without requiring the immediately preceding step.
If several steps in the same group are enabled, only one remains On and the later programmed instruction wins.
The selected step latches after input Off; enabling Syyy.00 clears the group.
constraints_en: yyy is the group number 0..127 and xx the step number 0..99. The operand is a BIT step-relay contact.
review_notes: This is the S-device last-input-priority instruction; do not equate its mnemonic template with arbitrary SFC graph-step insertion.

XORGMEX.purpose_en: Perform module-controlled homing from an LS servo touch-probe or index signal.

XGEARIP.purpose_en: Synchronize a follower speed at specified master and follower positions.
behavior_en: sl/ax select the module and follower axis. n1 is the REAL follower/master ratio; positive ratios follow the master direction and negative ratios reverse it.
n2 and n3 specify the master/follower synchronization positions (DINT); n4 is the master travel distance before synchronization (DINT). n5 selects master axis 1..8 or encoder1/2 as 9/10.
The operation can take multiple scans. The worked example starts synchronization at master position n2 minus n4.
constraints_en: Use a different network-connected master axis or an encoder; the master cannot be the command/follower axis. Zero ratio is prohibited; the page states nonzero -32,768..32,767.
The command cannot execute with M-code On (353), servo Off (354), invalid master selection (355), zero/out-of-range ratio (356), or follower speed above its limit (357).
Master homing prevents the command (358), except for the stated LS Mecapion L7N/L7NH/XIP master cases.
The ax convention 1..8 is for XGF-PN8B and must match the actual module. XBC-U/XBM can use XBF-PNxxB network positioning in slots 2/3 only.
review_notes: The Korean restriction calls the prohibited-zero quantity the master ratio, while the operand table exposes one synchronization ratio n1; preserve the stated zero/range condition without inventing a separate operand.
